question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Before proposing your ideas, list in the assumptions field the hidden assumptions built into this question and into the way the field usually tests it. Then propose your 5 ideas: each must test, exploit, or work around the failure of a different one of those assumptions, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

ideas.title: Clone-splitting twin assay to partition fate variance
ideas.description: Using heritable expressed barcodes or physical splitting of small clones, treat one half of each clone and profile or re-challenge the other half, then quantify how much of survival probability is shared within a lineage versus private to each cell, and how fast that shared component decays over passages. This directly measures whether 'priming' is a stable pre-existing property or a short-lived fluctuation, instead of assuming it.

ideas.title: Single-cell genome and ecDNA accounting of survivors
ideas.description: Run single-cell whole-genome sequencing plus DNA FISH for ecDNA and target-locus copy number on parental and surviving cells, with duplex sequencing of the drug target to detect mutations below 0.1% allele frequency. This tests whether the 'genetically identical' premise is false and whether rare copy-number or ecDNA jackpot cells, not transcriptional states, account for survival.

ideas.title: Per-cell intracellular drug dosimetry
ideas.description: Measure the actual drug concentration each cell receives using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, mass-spectrometry imaging, or a live target-engagement reporter, combined with per-cell efflux-pump activity, and correlate it with fate by live imaging. If survival tracks drug exposure rather than transcriptional state, the usual expression-based explanations are confounded by pharmacology.

ideas.title: Neighborhood-controlled survival mapping
ideas.description: Micropattern or seed cells at defined local densities, image the full field during treatment, and model each cell's survival as a function of its own state versus the number, proximity, and death timing of its neighbors; complement with conditioned-medium and apoptotic-debris transfer experiments. This tests whether survival is cell-autonomous at all or a property of local microenvironment and dying-neighbor signals.

ideas.title: Forced-state causal test with graded fate readout
ideas.description: Use CRISPRa/CRISPRi or an inducible/optogenetic construct to drive candidate primed-state genes in a titratable fraction of cells before treatment, and ask whether the surviving fraction shifts proportionally; score outcome not as live/dead but as a continuous live-imaging trajectory (death, arrest, dormancy, proliferation). This converts a correlative state into a causal dose-response and resolves whether 'survivors' are one population or several.

assumptions: Survivors are assumed to be 'pre-marked': a rare state exists before drug is added that deterministically specifies survival, rather than survival being decided stochastically during or after exposure.
The population is assumed genetically uniform, so rare subclonal mutations, aneuploidy, or ecDNA copy-number fluctuation are excluded by assertion rather than measured.

The causal variable is assumed to be transcriptional state, because scRNA-seq is the default instrument; protein, metabolic, and especially per-cell intracellular drug concentration are assumed uniform or merely downstream.
Survival is assumed cell-autonomous: a property of the single cell, not of its local density, neighbors, or signals released by the cells dying around it.

A destructive snapshot of the pre-treatment population is assumed to be informative about the specific cells that later survive, i.e. that state is stable and that measured cell and surviving cell can be linked.
Correlation between a pre-treatment state and survival is treated as causation, with few experiments that force cells into or out of the state and ask whether the surviving fraction moves.
Survival is assumed binary and survivors homogeneous (one state, one mechanism), ignoring graded outcomes such as dormancy, slow cycling, and multiple independent escape routes.
The clonal cell line under constant saturating drug is assumed to model fluctuating drug exposure in a tissue.
